{{short description|American mathematician (born 1941)}}
'''Kenneth C. Millett''' (born 1941) is a professor of mathematics at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]].<ref name="cv">[http://www.math.ucsb.edu/~millett/kcmwebSCV2014.html Curriculum vitae], retrieved 2015-02-09.</ref> His research concerns [[low-dimensional topology]], [[knot theory]], and the applications of knot theory to [[DNA]] structure;<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.cabinetmagazine.org/issues/20/wertheim.php|title=Where the Wild Things Are: An Interview with Ken Millett|first=Margaret|last=Wertheim|volume=20|journal=Cabinet Magazine|date=Winter 2005–2006}}.</ref> his initial is the "M" in the name of the [[HOMFLY polynomial]].<ref>{{citation|title=Knot Theory|first=Vassily|last=Manturov|publisher=CRC Press|year=2004|isbn=9780203402849|page=57|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=lRLwUP8LLLcC&pg=PA57}}.</ref>

Millett graduated from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1963 with a bachelor's degree in mathematics.<ref name="cv"/> He earned his Ph.D. in 1967 from the [[University of Wisconsin]] under the supervision of Edward R. Fadell.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=9033}}</ref> After short-term instructor positions at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] and MIT, he joined the UCSB faculty in 1969 and was promoted to professor in 1979.<ref name="cv"/>

Millett won the [[Carl B. Allendoerfer Award]] of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] in 1989 and the [[Chauvenet Prize]] in 1991 for a paper on knot theory with [[W. B. R. Lickorish]].<ref>[http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/writing-awards/the-new-polynomial-invariants-of-knots-and-links Writing Awards: The New Polynomial Invariants of Knots and Links], MAA, retrieved 2015-02-09.</ref><ref name="NewPolynomialInvariants">{{cite journal | last1=Lickorish | first1=W. B. R. | last2=Millett | first2=K. C. | title=The New Polynomial Invariants of Knots and Links | journal=Mathematics Magazine | publisher=Taylor & Francis | volume=61 | issue=1 | year=1988 | issn=0025-570X | doi=10.1080/0025570x.1988.11977338 | pages=3–23}}</ref>
He became a [[fellow]] of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 2000.<ref name="cv"/> In 2012, he became one of the inaugural fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2015-02-08.</ref>
